interval.printed: 95% intervals. Paired BCa bootstrap for the own-k votes, the Sonnet-low rows, the pieces counterparts and the effort pairs (B = 10,000, stamped on the effort pairs; not stamped on the other rows). Paired cluster bootstrap over puzzles for the Opus-against-Sonnet rows (draw count not stamped). Exact Clopper–Pearson for the post hoc per-setting intervals at the ceiling.

n.printed: puzzles per pair: 80; a vote uses k samples per puzzle (the k column); the other rows compare single-sample accuracies (for a Haiku setting, the mean over its samples)

set.printed: the Study 1 main-run puzzle set at 6 steps: each puzzle as a chain (1×6) and as pieces (6×1)

tier.printed: exploratory, unadjusted, outside Holm; the exact per-setting intervals at the ceiling are post hoc

columns.printed: Cost per correct answer ratio [95% interval]

notes.printed: Every comparison is exploratory, unadjusted and outside the Holm family: no verdict is printed. The status column repeats each block's stamped label.

The own-k votes use each Haiku setting's own cost-matched k against Opus-medium and against Sonnet-medium; where a k is capped, the Raw k column gives the cost-matched k before the cap. Capped, all against Opus-medium: Haiku-low on 6×1, held at the cap on k of 40 (raw k 46); Haiku, thinking off on 1×6 and 6×1, held at the cap on k of 40 (raw k 45 and 50); Haiku-max on 1×6 and 6×1, held at its 3 samples drawn (raw k 9 and 11). Against Sonnet-medium no k is capped. The spend share of a vote is its spend over the comparator's (the file's "spend ratio"), a point with no interval.

notes.formula: the spend share rounded to three decimals (what it would print without its fourth)
notes.printed: Spend shares print at three decimals; 0.9998 (Haiku-low vote against Opus-medium at 1×6) keeps a fourth decimal, because at three it would print as 1.000 and read as equal to the comparator's spend.

The pieces counterparts repeat Test 3's and Test 5's comparisons at 6×1. Test 4's comparison was not computed at 6×1 in the main run, because step voting did not run on pieces there. Step voting on pieces against one Opus-medium answer (the pieces counterpart of Test 4; unadjusted, exploratory, outside the pre-registered family) ran later, in the top-up run, and is reported in TAB-14.

Neither pieces counterpart is shown no worse (Holm-adjusted): both are outside the Holm family. The file's own "declared" field on the counterpart of Test 5 means its p fell below the one-sided level for that comparison alone, not under Holm, and is not shown.
Format compliance is the share of each side's samples in the required answer format; for a vote, that of the setting's samples the vote is drawn from.
Effort pairs are low effort minus medium effort at one sample; the cost difference is the stamped difference of the two mean list costs of one sample (in US dollars; for Opus, its one answer).

Where both settings of an effort pair are at the ceiling, the bootstrap interval of d collapses to one point (marked collapsed). The difference itself has no exact interval in free analysis 4, which gives each setting's exact 95% interval instead (Clopper–Pearson over puzzles), printed in that setting's accuracy cell as post hoc† (exact): a presentation only, not a test.

Opus-low against Sonnet-medium at 1×6 is Test 5's comparison. Its confirmatory d and interval are in TAB-02; the Opus-against-Sonnet block's separate exploratory interval for the same pair is not printed, and that row keeps the block's accuracies and cost ratios only. At 6×1 the same pair is the pieces counterpart of Test 5: its d and interval are printed once, in that row, and the Opus-against-Sonnet row keeps its accuracies and cost ratios only.

Dashes mark cells that do not apply (a spend share and a raw k belong to the votes, a cost ratio to the Opus-against-Sonnet rows), cells the files do not stamp (the k of the Opus-against-Sonnet rows and of the pieces counterpart of Test 5, and the cost difference in dollars of the Opus-against-Sonnet rows) and the d cells of the two Opus-against-Sonnet rows whose comparison is printed elsewhere. The cost columns are in a part of their own that prints only the rows with a cost figure, so the dashes of the other rows are not printed there; the accuracy columns are in two parts, one for the own-k votes and one for the other rows.
Sonnet-medium ran at medium effort, one level below Sonnet's default, in every row where it appears.
